added_models.model: IND-era in-vitro mitochondrial toxicity assay (HepG2 / CEM cell lines: mtDNA content, cytochrome c oxidase, cytotoxicity after 14-day exposure)

safety.confidence_note: abstract-level (PMID 20516278, epub 2010-06-01); Europe PMC renders the unit as 'microM'. The 1b MAD study had finished (AASLD 2009 abstract) but no safety comparison is stated.
safety.model: IND-era in-vitro mitochondrial toxicity assay (HepG2 / CEM cell lines: mtDNA content, cytochrome c oxidase, cytotoxicity after 14-day exposure)
safety.note: Pharmasset's cell-line mitochondrial-toxicity assay cleared PSI-7851 (sofosbuvir diastereomer mixture) at 100 uM; no patient safety data yet.
safety.quote: No cytotoxicity, mitochondrial toxicity, or bone marrow toxicity was associated with PSI-7851 at the highest concentration tested (100 μM).
safety.judgement: Opener at the first peer-reviewed use of the standard cell-line mitochondrial assay for a member. model_kind 'ex_vivo' because the enum has no cell-line value (same convention as the replicon track). model_filed true: the FDA Sovaldi pharm/tox review section 4.2 reviews these mtDNA/cytochrome c oxidase data.

safety.magnitude_basis: absence of mitochondrial-type harm (cardiomyopathy, lactic acidosis, myopathy) in the Phase 3 population vs a clean assay at 200 uM
safety.confidence_note: FDA review text read in full. The clinical side is in the same package: Medical Review section 2.4 'No safety issues related to cardiac toxicity have been noted in clinical development program of sofosbuvir to date.' registry_date is the FISSION results posting (NCT01497366), the earliest Phase 3 record.
safety.model: IND-era in-vitro mitochondrial toxicity assay (HepG2 / CEM cell lines: mtDNA content, cytochrome c oxidase, cytotoxicity after 14-day exposure)
safety.note: Sofosbuvir was clean in mtDNA synthesis, cytochrome c oxidase and host-polymerase assays to 200 uM; the FDA's focused cardiac review of the Phase 3 program found no signal.
safety.short: Clean mito assay, clean Phase 3 cardiac review
safety.quote: Sofosbuvir did not show evidence of mitochondrial toxicity in mitochondrial assays and did not inhibit host DNA or RNA polymerases at concentrations up to 200 μM.
safety.judgement: Scored 'same' on the same-package convention the draft uses for the toxicology track: the FDA reviewed the mitochondrial assays precisely because of the BMS-986094 class concern (Medical Review 2.4) and found the Phase 3 cardiac record clean. The prediction was 'no mitochondrial-type harm at clinical exposure' and it held. The 'same' is placed before the BMS-986094 contra of the same year because one drug's contra beats another's same on a track.

safety.confidence_note: Drafter pairing: model side Vernachio 2011 AAC (PMID 21357300, epub 2011-02-28; abstract-level), patient side the FDA Medical Review section 2.4 quoting the 2012-08-23 BMS release (the MedR sentence is itself a quotation of a tier-5 release). NCT01425970 is terminated 'due to safety reasons' with no results posted, so registry_date is null. The first source to state that the standard HepG2 assay is insensitive is Feng 2016 (epub 2015-11-23): PC-3 cells 'more than an order of magnitude more sensitive to mitochondrial toxicity than the commonly used HepG2 cells'.
safety.model: IND-era in-vitro mitochondrial toxicity assay (HepG2 / CEM cell lines: mtDNA content, cytochrome c oxidase, cytotoxicity after 14-day exposure)
safety.note: Vernachio 2011: 'No evidence of mitochondrial toxicity ... after 14 days of INX-08189 exposure in both HepG2 and CEM'; Aug 2012: nine patients hospitalised, one heart-failure death.
safety.short: HepG2/CEM assay cleared BMS-986094; heart failure
safety.quote: While the cause of these unexpected events, which involve heart and kidney toxicity, has not been definitively established, the Company has determined that it is in the best interest of patients to halt development of BMS-986094.
safety.judgement: Contra by the stated-prediction rule, not the silence rule: the assay explicitly predicted no mitochondrial toxicity for INX-08189, the only prospective statement on this system for the member, and the drug caused cardiomyopathy and renal injury, the harm class such assays exist to flag. Dated 2013, the earliest admissible pairing (the checker's own convention for the toxicology track); whether the clinical harm was mitochondrial was unresolved in 2013 (Feng 2016 showed BMS-986094 mitochondrial toxicity at 0.5-0.7 uM in PC-3 cells; Baumgart 2016 found no mtDNA depletion in monkeys), so a reader who requires the mechanism to be settled would date this 2015 on Feng 2016. Not scored: PSI-352938 and IDX-184 IND-era mitochondrial data (no public model-side source found); bemnifosbuvir's prospective clean prediction (Good 2020) matched 8-week patients but cannot turn a contra track back.

added_models.model: POLRMT incorporation assay plus PC-3/HepG2 mitochondrial protein-synthesis and respiration panel (built after the BMS-986094 failure)

safety.confidence_note: full text read via Europe PMC (PMC3499576, epub 2012-11-15). The paper cites the BMS-986094 discontinuation as motivation but makes no member-by-member comparison with patients.
safety.model: POLRMT incorporation assay plus PC-3/HepG2 mitochondrial protein-synthesis and respiration panel (built after the BMS-986094 failure)
safety.note: Cameron-lab POLRMT incorporation assay and MT4-cell 'mitovir score', built after the Aug 2012 BMS-986094 halt; all anti-HCV ribonucleotides tested were POLRMT substrates.
safety.short: POLRMT assay built after BMS-986094 halt
safety.quote: We show that all of the anti-HCV ribonucleoside analogues are substrates for human mitochondrial RNA polymerase (POLRMT) and eukaryotic core RNA polymerase II (Pol II) in vitro.
safety.judgement: Opener. Separate track from the IND-era cell-line assay under the run's track-identity rule: a different model (biochemical POLRMT incorporation plus sensitised cell lines, MT4 then PC-3) built after the clinic knew the answer, and a different prediction (POLRMT substrate efficiency maps to clinical adverse events). model_filed true because the FDA Sovaldi pharm/tox review section 4.2 cites this paper for GS-461203 being 'a weak substrate for mitochondrial RNA polymerase compared to some other HCV nucleotide inhibitors', a model-vs-model statement, not a patient comparison, so no status in 2013. retrodiction stays false on an untested opener (lint).

safety.magnitude_basis: POLRMT incorporation (BMS-986094 triphosphate 92% of GTP rate vs sofosbuvir 0.45% of UTP) and PC-3 mitochondrial CC50 (0.68 uM vs >100 uM), qualitative against the clinical outcome
safety.confidence_note: full text read via Europe PMC (PMC4750701, epub 2015-11-23, print Feb 2016). Same paper: 'mericitabine and sofosbuvir did not interact with PolRMT or cause mitochondrial toxicity, consistent with their progression into advanced clinical development.' Jin 2017 AAC (doi 10.1128/AAC.00492-17, PMID 28559253) extends the POLRMT substrate-specificity series on the same system with no status change, so it is folded here rather than entered.
safety.model: POLRMT incorporation assay plus PC-3/HepG2 mitochondrial protein-synthesis and respiration panel (built after the BMS-986094 failure)
safety.note: BMS-986094's triphosphate was a full POLRMT substrate and hit mitochondrial protein synthesis at 0.5-0.7 uM; sofosbuvir's was a poor substrate and clean, matching the clinic.
safety.short: POLRMT panel separates BMS-986094 from sofosbuvir
safety.quote: In conclusion, analogous to the role of mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma in toxicity caused by some 2′-deoxynucleotide analogs, there is an association between HCV NI that interact with PolRMT and the observation of adverse events.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction (built and run after the Aug 2012 events), so 'retro', never 'same'. Gilead authors, so the sofosbuvir half is the sponsor's own; the BMS-986094 half uses the published clinical halt. IDX-184 (same triphosphate as BMS-986094) showed 'minimal toxicity', which the paper attributes to inefficient activation in the cells studied; its patients never showed the harm before the class hold, so that pairing is consistent but changes nothing. Primary rat cardiomyocytes in the same panel (CC50 0.4 uM) are part of this system, not a separate track.

safety.confidence_note: full text read. Patient side: same paper, 'Development of PSI-938 (prodrug of 2'F,2'CMe guanosine) was discontinued due to the observation of hepatic toxicity in phase 2b', and the FDA Sovaldi Medical Review ('Due to ALT elevations associated with GS-0938', QUANTUM). No registry results for QUANTUM were looked up this session.
safety.model: POLRMT incorporation assay plus PC-3/HepG2 mitochondrial protein-synthesis and respiration panel (built after the BMS-986094 failure)
safety.note: PSI-352938 (GS-0938) stopped for ALT elevations in QUANTUM (Dec 2011); in the panel it was a poor POLRMT substrate and >100 uM in every mitochondrial, hepatocyte and cytotoxicity assay.
safety.quote: For example, despite having tested it in a comprehensive battery of biochemical and cell-based assays, we were unable to elucidate a mechanism for the clinically observed adverse hepatic effects observed with PSI-938.
safety.judgement: A retrodiction that failed to reproduce the human data is 'contra' (decision 10). The panel included primary human hepatocyte and HepG2/Huh-7 viability, so hepatotoxicity is a harm the system could have shown, and the authors say so themselves. One member's contra beats another's retro on the track, so the track reads contra from 2015. Alternative reading, not taken: a mitochondrial panel is silent by design on a CYP-mediated metabolite mechanism (Good 2020 later found O6-alkylguanine formation from PSI-938 with CYP3A4), which would leave the track at retro; the brief scores what the data showed, and the data cleared the drug.
safety.reason: Retro panel still missed PSI-352938 liver harm

safety.model: Recombinant human CYP3A4 metabolite-formation assay (mutagenic O6-alkylguanine nucleobase release from guanosine nucleotide prodrugs)
safety.confidence_note: full text read via NCBI PMC (PMC6949113, epub 2020-01-08). Sponsor (Atea) authors.
safety.note: Atea rhCYP3A4 assay: AT-511 (bemnifosbuvir) released no O6-alkylguanine, unlike PSI-938 and PSI-661; no bemnifosbuvir patient safety data beyond single doses yet.
safety.quote: Unlike the other potent guanosine analogs PSI-938 and PSI-661, no mutagenic O 6 -alkylguanine bases were formed when incubated with cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4
safety.judgement: Opener at the first published use of this system for a member. Distinct from the mitochondrial tracks: it reads a CYP-mediated metabolite mechanism (hepatotoxicity), not POLRMT or mtDNA. model_filed false: no regulator review of it found. retrodiction false on the opener (lint); the PSI-938 half is scored as retro in the next entry.

safety.model: Recombinant human CYP3A4 metabolite-formation assay (mutagenic O6-alkylguanine nucleobase release from guanosine nucleotide prodrugs)
safety.magnitude_basis: PSI-938 converted 31% (1.57 uM O6-ethylguanine from 5 uM) vs 0% for AT-511, qualitative against the known PSI-938 clinical hepatotoxicity
safety.confidence_note: sponsor-authored and hedged ('likely due to'); the PSI-938 ALT signal (QUANTUM, Dec 2011) is cited by the paper, not shown. The same assay also released O6-methylguanine from BMS-986094 (8.7%), whose patient harm was cardiac, which the paper does not discuss.
safety.note: Run eight years after PSI-938 stopped for ALT elevations: the assay attributes that hepatotoxicity to O6-alkylguanine release, which it reproduced in vitro.
safety.short: CYP3A4 assay reproduces PSI-938 liver signal
safety.quote: Other prodrugs of M3, such as PSI-661 and PSI-938, have been discontinued or have failed due to toxicity in the clinic likely due to the formation of mutagenic O 6 -alkylated nucleobase metabolites
safety.judgement: Retrodiction (PSI-938's clinical hepatotoxicity was public from 2011-2012), so 'retro', never 'same'. Low confidence because the mechanistic attribution is the sponsor's hedged reading; the FDA Sovaldi MedR names the GS-0938 ALT elevations on the patient side.

safety.model: Recombinant human CYP3A4 metabolite-formation assay (mutagenic O6-alkylguanine nucleobase release from guanosine nucleotide prodrugs)
safety.magnitude_basis: no mutagenic metabolite in vitro vs no drug-related serious adverse event or drug-related discontinuation in 275 patients over 8 weeks
safety.confidence_note: abstract-level (PMID 42826065, epub 2026-10-02); the abstract reports no drug-related SAEs but gives no liver-enzyme table, so the hepatic match is inferred from overall tolerability. Paired by us, sponsor on both sides.
safety.note: Prospective clean prediction for bemnifosbuvir held in an 8-week Phase 2 of 275 patients with ruzasvir: no drug-related serious adverse events.
safety.quote: No drug-related serious adverse events or premature treatment discontinuations due to drug-related adverse events were reported.
safety.judgement: Prospective: the CYP3A4 result (2020) preceded the Phase 2 (results posted 2025-10-21). Paired comparison, so comparison_stated false and model_src named. Dated to the peer-reviewed paper (2026) rather than the registry posting. Earlier 7-day MAD (Berliba 2019) is too short to test hepatotoxicity.

considered_not_added: IDX-184 mouse/rat/cynomolgus toxicology (Luo 2015, doi 10.1177/0960327115592939) and its 3-day monotherapy vs replicon (Lalezari 2012, doi 10.1128/AAC.01521-12): both belong to the existing rodent-dog-monkey-tox and hcv-replicon-huh7 tracks, not new systems; left for the draft's own entries per the task.

Patient-isolate NS5B shuttle-vector replicons (FDA CrossR: 'NS5B amplified from individual patient plasma samples and cloned into the replicon-based shuttle vectors'): a patient-level use, but the same Huh-7 replicon system already tracked as hcv-replicon-huh7.

HCV-infected chimpanzee: no member drug was tested in chimpanzees in any abstract found (the one hit is a 2026 veterinary report of DAA therapy in captive chimpanzees, after approval, with no prediction compared with patients).

Human-liver chimeric (uPA-SCID / humanized) mice: used with the non-member Gilead nucleotide GS-558093 (2015) and with sofosbuvir in post-approval Japanese combination/resistance studies (2016, 2019); no prospective or stated comparison for a member drug.

In-silico viral-kinetic and multiscale models (sofosbuvir; bemnifosbuvir 2026, doi 10.1002/cpt.70454): fitted to patient HCV RNA data, not preclinical models; sofosbuvir's 400 mg came from 3-day MAD kinetics and Phase 2, as the draft's dose judgement records.
Human challenge and human genetic models: none exist for HCV NS5B nucleotides.

Bemnifosbuvir (AT-527): Good 2020 made a fresh prospective prediction on the IND-era cell-line track ('did not ... elicit cytotoxicity or mitochondrial toxicity at concentrations up to 100 uM') and patients matched (7-day MAD well tolerated, Berliba 2019; 8-week Phase 2 NCT05904470, results posted 2025-10-21, Hepatology 2026: 'No drug-related serious adverse events'). Not entered: the track is contra on BMS-986094 and one drug's contra beats another's same, so a later 'same' entry would misstate the track's status; recorded here.
Jin 2017 AAC (POLRMT substrate specificity) and the Arnold 2012 MT4 'mitovir score': the same POLRMT system as the polrmt-mito-panel-retro track, no status change; folded into that track's notes.
Primary rat cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity (Feng 2016, CC50 0.4 uM for BMS-986094): part of the same Gilead panel, not split out; the human cardiomyocyte system is already the hipsc-cardiomyocyte track.
Baumgart 2016 monkey mtDNA (doi 10.1093/toxsci/kfw135): already cited in the draft's cyno-monkey-echo-retro judgement; same animals as Gill 2016.
ALS-2200/VX-135 (2013 liver-enzyme hold) and uprifosbuvir (MK-3682): no public model-side mitochondrial or toxicology source and no admissible patient-side source found this session; unscored.
PSI-352938 IND-era mitochondrial data (Pharmasset, 2010-2011): not verified this session, so its hepatotoxicity is scored only on the Feng 2016 retro panel, where the paper itself states the miss.

gaps.lead: IDX-184 on the replicon track (Lalezari 2012, -0.5 to -0.7 log10)
gaps.detail: Changes nothing scored: hcv-replicon-huh7 efficacy 2 stays same, no 'neg'. IDX-184 never failed in patients on efficacy: 3-day monotherapy -0.5 to -0.7 log10 at 25-100 mg vs placebo -0.05, authors call it 'significant antiviral activity' (Lalezari 2012, doi 10.1128/AAC.01521-12, PMID 23070151); 14-day IDX184 + P/R gave -2.7 to -4.3 log10 vs -1.5 for P/R alone, 'greater antiviral activity ... than P/R' (Antivir Ther 2013, doi 10.3851/imp2552, PMID 23439365). Luo 2015's 'suboptimal efficacy' is a sponsor statement in a toxicology paper beside the BMS-986094 regulatory hold, not a trial result; decision 13 judges neg on data, not on what the sponsor said. The draft judgement's 'no member failed on efficacy' could name IDX-184 as stopped on the class hold (note only).
